eligibility: UNHCR Tertiary Refugee Scholarship Programme (DAFI) offers qualified refugee and returnee (in selected countries) students the possibility to earn an undergraduate degree in their country of asylum or home country
DAFI covers programmes at International Standard Classification of Education (ISCED) level 6, or bachelor's or equivalent level, leading to a first degree or equivalent qualification
DAFI also covers short-cycle tertiary education at ISCED level 5, including accredited Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programmes of two years or more
DAFI does NOT cover Masters studies

official.description: Founded in 1992 as the Albert Einstein German Academic Refugee Initiative, DAFI is UNHCR's tertiary scholarship programme offering qualified refugee and returnee students the possibility to earn an undergraduate degree in their country of asylum or home country. The package covers a range of costs including tuition, fees, study materials, food, transportation, accommodation and other expenses, and the programme has supported over 27,200 students in 59 countries since its founding.
official.region: Global - multi-country programme delivered through UNHCR country operations and DAFI partners
official.program_type: UN agency tertiary scholarship (UNHCR Tertiary Refugee Scholarship Programme - DAFI)

verification.notes: Programme description, coverage wording, ISCED 5/6 eligibility rules and application steps verified live on the DAFI Programme Management Platform and the UNHCR programme page (both read in a rendered browser session after plain fetches were blocked). UNHCR publishes no global award amount, no global deadline and no single document list - these are set per country operation.

applicant_utility.summary: DAFI funds an undergraduate or two-year-plus TVET place you already hold (or can secure) locally - it will not send you abroad and it will not fund a master's degree, so admission to an eligible ISCED 5 or 6 programme in your country of asylum or home country comes first. Because no global deadline exists, the only date that matters is the one in your own UNHCR country operation's call, and the application itself is free and runs entirely through the DAFI Programme Management Platform. The package is built to remove the everyday barriers to studying: tuition, fees, study materials, food, transportation and accommodation, with preparatory, language and ICT courses added where the country operation has capacity. Places tightened after 2024, when UNHCR reported the first drop in scholar numbers since 2020, so treat each country window as a single annual shot.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Refugees registered with UNHCR (and returnees in selected countries) who hold a secondary-school qualification, have been admitted to a local bachelor's or accredited two-year-plus TVET programme, and need both tuition and living costs covered.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your own UNHCR country operation has an open DAFI call before investing time in the platform - the programme pages publish no deadline of their own
Secure your admission to an eligible local programme first; the scholarship follows the place, not the other way round
Check your course is ISCED 6 (bachelor's or equivalent) or an accredited ISCED 5 short-cycle/TVET programme of two years or more - master's degrees are excluded
Email the country contact listed on the DAFI platform to confirm that country's document list and window
Register on the platform with an email address you check regularly and save the application in-progress as you build it
common_rejection_risks: Applying for a master's programme, which DAFI explicitly does not cover
Proposing a course shorter than two years or a non-accredited TVET programme outside ISCED 5/6
Assuming a global deadline exists and missing your country operation's own window
Starting the platform application before admission to an eligible programme is secured
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything beyond tuition, fees, study materials, food, transportation and accommodation: the package is defined per country operation, so personal, medical, family and programme-specific extra costs must be funded from other sources.
document_audit: The platform publishes no universal document list - required documents come from your country operation's call, so another country's checklist is not evidence
Request certified copies of your secondary-school and admission documents as soon as a call opens rather than at submission time
Keep proof of UNHCR registration accessible; country operations screen on registration status before academic review
alerts: There is no global DAFI deadline - a missed country window generally means waiting for the next cycle
Returnees are only eligible in selected countries; in most operations you must be a refugee living in the country of asylum
Scholar numbers fell in 2024 for the first time since 2020 amid reduced global funding, so competition per place is tighter than in peak years
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the DAFI Programme Management Platform, build and save the application in-progress, submit it online for review, and wait for the outcome; questions go to the country contact email listed on the platform or your nearest UNHCR office or DAFI partner.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a one-year senior placement inside a principal's office, not a scholarship: the contract is non-renewable, creates no right to employment, and the entire application is the host's online form plus a CV, transcripts and three recommendation letters. The $100,000 stipend is paid monthly by the host, but you must arrange your own medical insurance, child education and retirement cover because host staff schemes do not extend to Fellows. Selection is unusually top-heavy - host HR shortlists ten files, the Foundation reviews them, and the head of the host makes the final pick from three - so your file has to read like a candidate for the principal's office rather than for a vacancy notice. The AfDB route closes 20 November 2026, and the ITC and UNECA routes run on their own systems with their own dates.
applicant_utility.best_fit: African nationals under 40 (45 for women with children) with a master's degree, at least seven years of relevant experience and private-sector or policy-analytics depth who want a year working at the most senior level of a continental institution.
application_readiness_checklist: Pick your host route first - AfDB, ITC and UNECA run separate application systems with separate closing dates
Rebuild your CV around the host's current priorities (for AfDB 2027: large-scale resource mobilisation, financial-architecture reform, the demographic dividend, climate-resilient infrastructure)
Line up three referees early; three letters of recommendation are mandatory and are the slowest item to collect
Request academic transcripts well ahead of the closing date, as university transcript offices are slow in October

Clear the hard bars before investing time (AfDB route): not a current, former, retired or separated Bank staff member, no close family ties to staff, and not a government official, active military member or political party leader
common_rejection_risks: Missing that the three routes use different systems and deadlines, and applying to the wrong one
Submitting a generic academic CV instead of an executive CV that states date of birth, nationality, education and relevant experience
Attaching fewer than three letters of recommendation, or letters that arrive after the closing date
Thin evidence of private-sector experience and quantitative or development-model skills, which the AfDB route names as key competences
Falling outside the age limit: 40, extended to 45 only for women with children
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Medical insurance, child education and retirement arrangements: the Fellow is excluded from the host's child educational scheme, staff medical insurance and retirement plans, and the Foundation only ensures the Fellow makes their own arrangements. Assumption-of-duty and repatriation travel and shipping are covered, as are official mission travel and travel insurance.
document_audit: The CV must explicitly state date of birth, nationality, education and relevant experience - an incomplete CV is a vetting-stage failure
Three separate letters of recommendation are mandatory; brief referees on the specific host route and its stated priorities
Academic transcripts are required as copies; start the request early rather than in the final week of the window
alerts: The fellowship is not renewable and confers no right to employment; on the AfDB route you cannot be recruited as Bank staff for one year after it ends
The age cut-off is strict: 40, or 45 only for women with children
The AfDB states it never asks for payments of any kind during recruitment and never requests bank account details - treat any such request as fraud
Only applicants who fully meet the requirements and are considered for interview are contacted, so silence means the file did not clear vetting
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Online only, through the chosen host's own system (the AfDB vacancy page for the Abidjan route): submit the form with CV, academic transcripts and three recommendation letters by the closing date, after which HR shortlists ten, the Foundation reviews, and three candidates go to the head of the host for final selection.
